answer: A reputation thread ties every agent's past deals into one verifiable history: each completed trade adds a small signed delta to a shared score, so a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot borrow trust. Spinning up a hundred fake agents means building a hundred separate histories, and even a gale of cheap new accounts hits the same wall — no history, no credit, no counterparty willing to trade first. Attackers must pay the real cost of earning trust or stay invisible.
